`agent-pipeline run` (run <runId>, pid <pid>) will stop once the Tickets it holds are finished. It claims no more.
Ctrl+C in that Run's own terminal stops it at once instead, at the cost of killing the Stages it is running and leaving their Tickets stranded for the next Run.

Two lines on stdout, and exit code 0: the Stop reached the process the Run lock
names. The first says which Run was asked, in the three things the lock knows
about it — the command line it was started with, its run id and its process id.
The second is the alternative and its price, because a human who wants a Run to
end now reaches for the terminal it is running in anyway, and what that costs is
the one thing about a Stop worth saying twice.

Everything else is one line on stderr with exit code 2 and no signal sent. No
Run holds the lock, or the Run on this Host it names is gone:

No Run to stop: nothing holds the Run lock on the `agent-pipeline/lock` branch, or the Run on this Host that left it there is gone. A lock like that is the next Run's to reclaim, so nothing here removes it.

One line for both, because they are one thing to whoever asked: there is nobody
to stop. A dead lock is left exactly where it is — reclaiming one belongs to the
next Run that starts, not to a command that only reads.

A Run on another Host is named rather than signalled, because a Stop is a
signal to a process and only the Host the Run is on can send one (ADR-0006).
The Host is the workstation by its hostname, or the cloud Host by its session:

`agent-pipeline run` (run <runId>) holds the Run lock from <the workstation `<hostname>` | the cloud Host of session `<session>`>, started <startedAt>. Only that Host can send it a Stop: `agent-pipeline stop` there, or its Operator on a cloud Host. Nothing was sent.

A `ticket <n>` holding the lock is named rather than signalled, since a Run
given one Ticket takes no more whatever happens:

`agent-pipeline ticket 5` (run <runId>, pid <pid>) holds the Run lock, and a Run given one Ticket ends with it anyway. Nothing was sent.

A signal that could not be delivered — the Run ended between the liveness check
and the SIGTERM, or it belongs to a user this shell may not signal — says why:

Could not ask `agent-pipeline run` (run <runId>, pid <pid>) to stop: <reason>

There is no stop file, so nothing here is written and nothing is read back: a
second `stop` prints exactly what the first did, and the Run ignores the second
signal (ADR-0006).
